title: [finding] `os generate object NAME` in an `os init -t app` project writes `name: 'NAME'` with no namespace prefix, so the next `os validate` refuses the object the CLI just generated
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**, `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` (the `object` generator's `name` value). Finding class **(a)**, with `reach:` measured at a public door (`os generate` → `os validate`).

Found by the `os-dev` round on #19722 (PR #20195), which measured it and left it unchanged (outside its surface). Filed by the `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024, `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP`). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens (measured by the #19722 dev on a CLI built at `origin/main` `3bd28e2b`)

1. `os init my-app -t app`
2. `os g object order_line` writes an object with `name: 'order_line'`.
3. `os validate` exits 1 and `os compile` exits 2, both with 「Object 'order_line' is missing the package namespace prefix. Rename it to 'my_app_order_line' (namespace = 'my_app')」.

The documented example in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`'s `os generate` section, `os g object customer`, lands the same way. So an author (or an AI) following the page gets a refusal from the platform's own gate on the platform's own generated output. PR #20195 changes the object's declaration SHAPE, not its name, and does not change this.

## The contract it contradicts

- The platform's own author-time refusal: an object in a namespaced package must carry the `NAMESPACE_` prefix. The scaffolder emits what that gate refuses.
- `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, road step ①: 「一条命令起一个项目:脚手架、装好、验证通过」. Generation is part of that first step, and its output does not validate.

## Direction (for the claimant, ⛔ not a ruling)

`os generate object` should derive the prefix from the project's manifest namespace, the same one the refusal names. The PM has NOT measured which generator input carries it (`generate.ts`'s name handling beside `toSnakeCase`), nor whether the other generators that emit a machine name share the gap. A pin: generate, then validate, is green in a fresh `os init` app. The closed #10712 fixed the same prefix gap for the external object-draft door. That precedent is worth reading.

## Who acts

The `domain:cli` execution seat. It edits `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`, which PR #20195 (#19722) holds until it merges, and #19098 is queued behind it on the same file.

## Dedupe

MCP issue search in this repository, open and closed, run 2026-09-27: `os generate object missing package namespace prefix os validate fails after os init` → 10 hits, 1 open (#19722, the declaration-shape card, not this defect). The closest closed hit is #10712 (the external object-draft output lacked the prefix: the same class on a different emitter). The others (#19577, #17069, #16541, #16485, #15976, #11598, #11727, #9666) are other `os init` / `os generate` defects, all closed.

Dedupe words: `os generate object namespace prefix` · `missing the package namespace prefix` · `os g object customer validate` · `generate.ts manifest namespace`
